# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 67 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_067_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 67

**1** Jesus said: "Whoever knows all but is lacking in himself is lacking everything."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"In himself"** — *mmoq* is the key: external omniscience paired with interior deficit equals total poverty. EMET and LOGOS preserve this; PNEUMA's "self-knowledge" is an interpretation rather than a translation.

**"Lacking"** — EMET preferred over "deficient" (LOGOS) — more natural English; "lacking" also echoes the deficiency theme in Saying 70.

**Theological Note:** This is the Thomasine epistemological thesis in miniature: the goal of the gospel is not cosmological knowledge but self-knowledge leading to knowledge of the Father (cf. Saying 3: "know yourselves"). No Synoptic parallel exists. The saying stands as a programmatic statement.
